answer: In an attestation graph, trust is estimated by bounded random walks, so influence depends on paths into well-connected regions, not the number of claimed identities. A Sybil cluster connected by few attestations has low conductance—a narrow harbor against the tide. Under fixed edge-weight and mixing assumptions, cut and transitivity bounds limit the walk mass it can capture, bounding its aggregate voting weight; reaching a summit of influence requires credible links across the cut.
